messages:
IncidentsBot: Pager: dedicated-capacity-alert -> dedicated-eu-1 pool at 100% GPU utilization. Autoscaler failed to scale past 16 nodes (max reached). Queue depth rising: ~1.2k pending requests. Multiple reserved enterprise tenants affected; throttling detected. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/1938800000 :sparkles:
Alex: ack — I'm on call. putting a debrief here.
Raj: seeing multiple customer tickets about 503s from AcmeCorp and BetaFin. marking high impact.
Maya: pinging eng-runtime to check allocation failures. I see repeated errors in autoscaler logs: "AllocationError: nodeCreationQuotaExceeded" around 1938799950 onward.
Alex: good find. can we confirm provider quota? Liam, can you check cloud provider quotas and recent API errors?
Liam: looking. cloud API returns 403 / quotaExceeded for createInstance on the provider account used for dedicated-eu-1. also saw ~30 creation attempts failed.
Tina: so autoscaler tried to add nodes but hit a provider quota. that explains max-notes-not-actually-configured. can we temporarily raise provider quota or switch to a different AZ?
Maya: raising provider quota needs support ticket with provider (takes 30-60m). we should pursue immediate mitigations: 1) throttle noisy tenants, 2) route enterprise tenants to hosted fallback, 3) evict non-reserved batch jobs.
Alex: agreed. executing mitigation checklist.
Alex: action: apply per-tenant emergency throttle to tenant:beta-fin and tenant:research-batch (no SLA) to free up slots. command: `rbacctl limit set --tenant research-batch --gpu 0.2`
Tina: will start eviction of batch queues now. ETA ~2m for first wave to drain.
Raj: Support will contact affected customers with templated notice. Kelly (AM) please loop in AcmeCorp and BetaFin execs.
Kelly: on it. I'll send customer notice now and offer hosted-fallback with temporary credits.
EngRuntimeBot: Observability: model-serving queue breakdown: reserved-tenant AcmeCorp 42% of queued tokens, BetaFin 28%, research-batch 12%, other 18%. KV cache pressure moderate.
Maya: we can enable routing policy that falls back reserved tenants to hosted-api for critical requests. runtime flag: `enable_fallback_route --pool dedicated-eu-1 --tenants AcmeCorp,BetaFin --target hosted-eu-1`
Alex: do it but limit to critical routes that are sensitive to latency. avoid routing bulk background inference.
Maya: enabled fallback for `predict` and `chat` endpoints for AcmeCorp/BetaFin. traffic % forwarded: 30% initially.
Raj: ticket update: AcmeCorp reports partial restoration for some endpoints, still seeing elevated latencies for long-context calls.
Liam: provider support ticket created, but they acknowledged quota limit. They can temporarily allow burst if we provide justification; ETA 40m.
Tina: continuing evictions. freed 3 nodes worth of GPUs by killing low-priority jobs — reclaimed ~12% capacity. queue depth dropped from 1.2k -> 850.
Alex: good. next: can we adjust autoscaler config to more aggressively reuse preemptible nodes rather than creating new?
Maya: yes, switching to preemptible-first policy now: `rci autoscaler update --pool dedicated-eu-1 --policy preemptible-first` — flipping.
EngRuntimeBot: policy applied. monitoring for stability.
Alex: rolling manual scale override to bump cluster max to 20 while provider quota pending (this will place a request but may still be blocked). Command: `rci pool set --name dedicated-eu-1 --max-nodes 20 --override-reason "incident 1938800000"`
Liam: attempted override returned provider error as expected; no new nodes created.
Tina: with throttles + evictions + fallback routing we should keep critical tenants online while provider works quota. recommend keeping throttles in place until provider confirms.
Kelly: AcmeCorp update: execs asked for regular updates every 15m and requested a post-incident RCA. I'm coordinating.
Raj: raising incident priority to P1 due to enterprise customer impact and SLAs.
Alex: assigning owners: Alex (incident lead), Maya (runtime mitigation), Liam (cloud quota contact), Tina (evictions & capacity recapture), Raj (customer comms), Kelly (account).
Alex: quick checklist next: 1) continue evictions, 2) keep fallback routing, 3) support to notify customers, 4) attempt provider quota increase, 5) prepare postmortem with root cause hypothesis (quota not aligned with reserved needs + noisy neighbor usage spikes).
Maya: also enabling temporary per-tenant fair-share with strict caps to limit single-tenant spikes: `runtimectl fairshare set --pool dedicated-eu-1 --tenant AcmeCorp --cap 60%`
Alex: note — cap applied. watch for customer complaints.
EngRuntimeBot: after throttles and fallbacks: queued requests 850 -> 420 over ~8m. average P95 latency for routed requests to hosted-fallback: 1800ms.
Raj: Support: creating high-priority incident tickets for AcmeCorp and BetaFin, linking to this thread.
Liam: provider replied: they can increase quota by 10 nodes within 20-30m if we open a billing-backed escalation. starting that process now.
Tina: once quota increase goes through, autoscaler should be able to create nodes and drain queue. we should plan a controlled scale up rather than let autoscaler spam requests.
Maya: prepping controlled scale up script: ```
for i in 1..10
  rci node create --pool dedicated-eu-1 --type gpu-nv48
  sleep 10
end
```
Alex: hold on automated nodes until provider confirms. continue manual mitigations.
Kelly: customers updated. asking if we can fast-track dedicated-eu-1 capacity for AcmeCorp — Sales asks for a short-term reserved burst (paid).
Raj: noted. I'll track the request with billing & sales.
Alex: summary for incident timeline: 1938800000 root alert -> 1938800060 throttles + evictions + fallback applied -> 1938800300 queue reduced to ~420 -> 1938800600 provider escalated, ETA capacity +10 nodes in ~20-30m.
Tina: monitoring. I'll post when the first reclaimed GPU becomes available and confirm queues draining below 50.
Maya: logging mitigation steps for postmortem. please add any anomalous logs to the incident doc (link above).
Alex: thanks team. keeping this thread pinned for the incident. we'll switch to postmortem channel after recovery. :white_check_mark:
